CE attends port opening ceremony
body:
The opening ceremony of the redeveloped Huanggang Port was held today at the Huanggang Port Mainland Port Area, with the facility set to officially open at 6.30am tomorrow.

 

Chief Executive John Lee officiated at the ceremony alongside Director of the Guangdong Provincial People’s Congress Standing Committee Huang Chuping; CPC Guangdong Provincial Committee Standing Committee Member and CPC Shenzhen Municipal Committee Secretary Jin Lei; CPC Shenzhen Municipal Committee Deputy Secretary and Mayor of the Shenzhen Municipal Government Li Yun; Deputy Director of the Liaison Office of the Central People’s Government in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Luo Yonggang; Director General of the Guangdong Sub-Administration of the General Administration of Customs of the People’s Republic of China Zhang Geping; Director of Bureau III of CPC Central Committee’s Hong Kong & Macao Work Office and State Council’s Hong Kong & Macao Affairs Office Zou Jinsong; and Deputy Director of the Department of Border Security Check of the National Immigration Administration Mo Haiying.

 

The redevelopment of the port signifies the proactive alignment of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government with national development strategies, fulfilling goals to strengthen regional infrastructure connectivity under the National 15th Five-Year Plan. Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan, announced last month, explicitly set out to leverage the strengths of the redeveloped port by implementing a co-location arrangement and adopting a novel “collaborative inspection and joint clearance” mode.

 

The official opening marks a major milestone for Hong Kong and Shenzhen in enhancing the layout of boundary control points, improving clearance efficiency, and facilitating the cross-boundary flow of people. Speaking at the ceremony, Mr Lee described the project as a landmark undertaking built upon a close partnership and concerted efforts between Hong Kong and Shenzhen for shared benefits.

 

Mr Lee added that the official opening reflects a new height for connectivity within the Greater Bay Area, demonstrating “hard connectivity” in infrastructure, “soft connectivity” of rules and mechanisms, and a “connectivity of hearts” between the residents of the Mainland and Hong Kong. Positioned as the most important 24-hour passenger land boundary control point between the two cities, the redeveloped port has a design capacity of 200,000 passenger trips per day.

 

This capacity could further increase to about 300,000 trips daily upon the future commissioning of the MTR Corporation’s Northern Link Spur Line. Backed by the central authorities, the site implements a co-location arrangement with clearly delineated Hong Kong and Mainland port areas.

 

It is also the first land boundary control point between Hong Kong and Shenzhen to adopt the “collaborative inspection and joint clearance” mode, which significantly enhances the passenger experience. Under this new mechanism, clearance times will be significantly reduced from around 30 minutes at the original Lok Ma Chau/Huanggang Port to approximately five minutes.

 

Since the establishment of the Huanggang Port Hong Kong Port Area on July 31, the Hong Kong SAR Government has been pressing ahead at full steam with various preparatory tasks. Having confirmed operational readiness, Hong Kong and Shenzhen issued a joint statement on October 9, announcing that the port will officially open at 6.30am on October 12 to provide 24-hour clearance services for passengers and passenger vehicles.

 

Hong Kong SAR Government officials attending today’s ceremony included Chief Secretary Chan Kwok-ki, Financial Secretary Paul Chan, Secretary for Justice Paul Lam, Secretary for Security Tang Ping-keung, Secretary for Health Prof Lo Chung-mau, Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn, Secretary for Transport & Logistics Mable Chan, Secretary for Constitutional & Mainland Affairs Janice Tse, Commissioner of Police Chow Yat-ming, Director of Immigration Benson Kwok, Commissioner of Customs & Excise Chan Tsz-tat, and Director of the Chief Executive’s Office Carol Yip.

title: Autonomous car trial runs smoothly
body:
Members of the Autonomous Vehicle Applications Promotion Working Group today visited an autonomous vehicle (AV) trial in Tung Chung, North Lantau.

 

They received a briefing by the pilot proprietor on the trial’s progress before taking the AVs in batches to tour the Tung Chung Town Centre vicinity. Group members were pleased to note the stable, safe and smooth performance of the vehicles throughout the journey.

 

The Transport Department said that this is the working group’s first on-site visit to an AV trial. It noted that the visit helps members, comprising autonomous driving researchers, information technology professionals, and other experts and stakeholders, engage directly with the pilot proprietor.

 

The department encourages the proprietor to optimise technologies based on feedback from passengers in test rides. This continuous refinement aims to deliver a convenient travel experience genuinely felt by the public.

title: Arrangements ready for new port
body:
The Government today outlined the comprehensive arrangements for the opening of the new Huanggang Port, which is scheduled to commence operation at 6.30am on October 12.

 

Immigration clearance services at the port will start from 6.30am on that day. Prior to this switchover time, all passengers must continue to use the Lok Ma Chau Control Point to travel between Hong Kong and Shenzhen.

 

The Immigration Department (ImmD) will ensure that all passengers arriving at the Lok Ma Chau Control Point or the temporary port building of the Huanggang Port in Shenzhen before 6.30am will be able to complete their immigration clearance procedures.

 

The ImmD appealed to eligible Hong Kong residents to enrol for the new “collaborative inspection” automated channels in advance via the “HK e-Channel” mobile application.

 

To closely monitor operations and ensure timely response measures, the ImmD will set up a joint command centre with relevant departments, including the Hong Kong Police Force (HKPF), the Customs & Excise Department (C&ED) and the Transport Department (TD). It will also maintain close liaison with Mainland authorities, including the Shenzhen General Station of Exit & Entry Frontier Inspection.

 

Meanwhile, the C&ED reminded travellers that a “passenger-vehicle separation” arrangement will be implemented at the new Huanggang Port. Under this measure, general passengers in cross-boundary private vehicles must disembark at the drop-off area, carrying their personal luggage and belongings to the immigration clearance hall to undergo clearance procedures.

 

Outbound vehicles will first pass through the “customs front kiosk” for risk assessment, and vehicles requiring further inspection must proceed to the designated examination area.

 

The HKPF said it will implement crowd management measures, regulate traffic flow and facilitate on-site media activities to ensure public safety and smooth port operations. On the night of the switchover, the HKPF will set up a Joint Operation Centre at the new port to monitor the crowd and traffic movements in real time.

 

Officers will also be deployed to the Lok Ma Chau Control Point and the San Tin Public Transport Interchange (PTI) to manage crowds, as members of the public and bus enthusiasts are expected to gather to catch the first and last bus departures or photograph the old facilities before they cease operations.

 

Regarding public transport arrangements, the TD announced that the final northbound Lok Ma Chau-Huanggang cross-boundary shuttle bus, commonly known as the Yellow Bus, to the original Huanggang Port will depart from San Tin PTI between 6.15am and 6.20am on October 12. The final southbound Yellow Bus from the original port will depart only after all cross-boundary travellers who entered the original port before 6.30am have completed clearance and boarded.

 

For the five short-haul cross-boundary coach routes, the last northbound departures from urban areas to the original port will take place between 5.15am and 5.45am on October 12. The final southbound departures from the original port back to urban areas will be between 6.15am and 6.30am that morning.

 

For the opening, five franchised bus and three green minibus daytime routes will begin operating to the new Huanggang Port, with the earliest departures from their urban termini starting from 4.45am.

title: Huanggang Port to open Monday
body:
The Huanggang Port will officially open and commence operations at 6.30am on October 12, following an agreement between the Guangdong and Hong Kong governments.

 

The Security Bureau and the Office of Port of Entry & Exit of the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government jointly issued a notice on the port opening today.

 

Acceptance inspections of the new port building have been completed. Following the completion of a series of system tests, trials and emergency drills by both Hong Kong and Shenzhen, it has been confirmed that the port is ready for opening.

 

The facility will commence operation on October 12, providing 24-hour clearance services for passengers and passenger vehicles. At the same time, passenger clearance services between the temporary port building of the Huanggang Port in Shenzhen and the Lok Ma Chau Control Point in Hong Kong will be suspended.

 

Pursuant to the “Official Reply of the State Council concerning the Agreement on the Commissioning of the Huanggang Port Hong Kong Port Area & Related Extended Areas”, the Huanggang Port Hong Kong Port Area & Related Extended Areas were commissioned beginning at 00:00 hours on July 31, 2026, and are subject to the jurisdiction of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region in accordance with its laws.

 

The official opening date was determined by the governments of Guangdong and Hong Kong.

title: FS bound for Nanjing
body:
Financial Secretary Paul Chan will depart for Nanjing tomorrow morning to promote Hong Kong’s unique advantages as an international platform for Mainland enterprises. The delegation includes representatives from public organisations, innovation and technology (I&T) parks and professional bodies, as well as various business sectors.

 

On October 13, the delegation will attend a promotion conference in Nanjing themed “Jiangsu-Hong Kong Partnership: Setting Sail Together”. A series of business-matching and promotional activities will showcase how Hong Kong’s diverse financial and professional services can support overseas expansion.

 

The delegation will also highlight Hong Kong’s I&T ecosystem to foster resource matching and explore co-operation in technology research and development (R&D). To exchange experiences, members will visit local technology transfer institutions alongside green technology and biotechnology enterprises in Jiangsu Province.

 

During his stay in Nanjing, Mr Chan will deliver a keynote speech at Nanjing University and visit its frontier technology research institutes. He will also meet Hong Kong business people and residents living in Jiangsu to learn about their daily lives and business operations.

 

Furthermore, the finance chief will meet leaders of Jiangsu Province and Nanjing City to discuss strengthening economic, trade and I&T co-operation. Mr Chan will return to Hong Kong on Wednesday afternoon, during which time Deputy Financial Secretary Michael Wong will act as Financial Secretary.

title: AI powers solo startup success
body:
Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) is revolutionising the way entrepreneurs operate.

 

Jeffrey Yang, formerly a construction tech entrepreneur from Shanghai, moved to Hong Kong to pursue a doctorate in real estate and construction. When he saw how many of the city’s buildings were ageing, he set out to create an AI platform to make building management more efficient.

 

“We typically use panoramic cameras and drones to detect building issues like exterior wall cracks or water leakage,” Mr Yang explained. He pointed out that Hong Kong has more than 20,000 buildings over 30 years old, a factor that makes manual analysis both manpower- and resource-intensive.

 

"I have trained the AI on mandatory repair notices and regulations so it helps identify issues. Through the platform, building owners can understand their building’s condition well in advance and meet compliance requirements after repairs."

 

One-person results 

Traditional business ventures, regardless of their scale, often require hiring staff, leasing premises and developing complex systems, usually requiring at least 10 people to get things off the ground.

 

However, by joining Cyberport’s OPC (one-person company) Hub – an incubator designed specifically for one-person companies – Mr Yang is bringing his visions to life with just one person and a single computer. He said the Government’s free spatial data has provided a significant advantage, drastically reducing the costs and difficulties typically associated with data collection.

 

"I need to build city-scale spatial scenes in the early stages. Few cities worldwide offer open 3D spatial data, but with Hong Kong’s recent 3D photography publicly available, I am able to use a large amount of open data."

 

Every day, Mr Yang develops his platform within the co-working space of the OPC Hub. He manages a suite of AI agents, each handling a different task – from data analysis and building inspections to repair co-ordination and equipment maintenance.

 

Empowering innovation

Since its launch in July this year, the OPC Hub has received over 40 applications, with more than 30 companies already approved to join.

 

These companies span various sectors, including proptech, creative design, financial trading, education and cybersecurity. The talent pool is evenly split, with local entrepreneurs making up roughly half the cohort, and Mainland and overseas talent comprising the remainder.

 

"OPC could be a small team of one to 10. Whether pursued full-time or part-time, it is easy to test ideas and the cost of trial and error is very low,” explained Cyberport Chief Executive Officer Rocky Cheng, who noted that OPCs benefit from low overhead and rapid startup times.

 

“A small handful of people can now drive 10, dozens or even hundreds of AI agents to assist with product design, website development, marketing, data analysis, financial management and customer service."

 

He said that as long as the founders identify pain points or come up with innovative ideas that are well-received in the market, investors will take notice because investing at this stage is more cost-effective.

 

Beyond standard support, such as entrepreneurship training, business and investor matching, and professional services, the OPC Hub also provides AI technology facilitators, including discounted tokens, computing power, cloud services and cybersecurity consultations. This comprehensive support helps founders prioritise data privacy, permissions and AI security from the outset, enabling them to turn their concepts into market-trusted solutions.

 

Mr Cheng said this entrepreneurial trend is already taking off in the Mainland, and he believes it is set to experience similar growth in Hong Kong.

title: HK ranked world's freest economy
body:
The Fraser Institute’s Economic Freedom of the World 2026 Annual Report has once again ranked Hong Kong as the world's freest economy. Among the five areas of assessment in the report, the city maintained its top position in "Freedom to trade internationally" and secured second place in "Regulation".

 

The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government noted that the report reaffirmed Hong Kong's strengths as a free-market economy, alongside its open, efficient and fair business environment.

 

Amid growing economic uncertainties and rising trade protectionism, Hong Kong remains firmly committed to maintaining its free port status, zero-tariff policy and simple, low tax regime. These factors provide a secure, stable, fair, predictable and internationalised business and investment environment for entrepreneurs and investors worldwide.

 

The Hong Kong SAR Government added that as the country remains committed to high-standard, two-way opening up and continues to achieve breakthroughs in technological innovation, it serves as a major stabilising force and driving engine for global economic growth. Under the “one country, two systems” framework, Hong Kong enjoys the strong support of the motherland while maintaining close connections with the rest of the world.

 

While offering convenient access to both the Mainland and international markets, Hong Kong continues to practise common law in both Chinese and English. It also provides financial, shipping, trading and professional services that align seamlessly with international best standards, supported by an efficient government structure and a clean, professional civil service.

 

The Hong Kong SAR Government pointed out that these unique strengths enable Hong Kong to fully leverage its roles as a super connector and super value-adder, making it the premier gateway for Mainland enterprises to enter international markets and vice versa.

 

So far this year, Hong Kong has continued to scale new heights across various international competitiveness rankings spanning finance, innovation and technology, education and talent. This reflects wide recognition by the international community of Hong Kong's core strengths and the Hong Kong SAR Government's efforts to promote high-quality social and economic development.

 

Looking ahead, with the staunch support of the country, the Hong Kong SAR Government will continue to work alongside all sectors of the community to further enhance Hong Kong's roles as "four centres and one hub". It will accelerate the development of the Northern Metropolis to inject stronger impetus into social and economic growth, open up broader development prospects for local enterprises and the public while providing greater opportunities for enterprises, investors and talent worldwide.
